faq: Do I need an audit before a roadmap?
It helps but is not required. If you have no audit, we run a short discovery chat first and base the roadmap on that. Larger roadmaps benefit from a full audit.
Will the roadmap include specific vendors?
It names tool types and a few example options where useful. We are independent and take no commission, so the choice stays yours.
How accurate are the cost ranges?
They are estimates from public pricing and typical effort, shown as ranges. Final costs depend on your volume and the tools you pick, so we mark each as low, likely or high.
Can you help carry out the plan?
Yes. Each initiative can be quoted as its own fixed price job. You can also give the roadmap to your own team or another provider to carry out.

desc:
An AI roadmap for the next six months lays out what to do, in which order, who owns each step and roughly what it costs. Ecom Swift LLC turns your goals, team and budget into a clear plan with checkpoints, so you never try everything at once.

## What is an AI roadmap?

An AI roadmap is a written plan that shows how your business will adopt AI over a set period, usually three to six months. It lists the initiatives you will carry out, puts them in order, names an owner for each and gives a cost range. It also marks checkpoints where you decide whether to continue, adjust or stop.

A roadmap is different from a list of ideas. A list says what is possible. A roadmap says what happens first, what depends on what, and who is responsible.

## Why a plan matters more than a tool list

Without a plan, AI adoption turns into a series of unrelated experiments. One person signs up for a tool, another builds a small automation, a third pastes data into something nobody approved. Money and attention spread thin, and nothing is finished.

A roadmap fixes this by setting an order. Early steps prepare the ground, for example tidying data or agreeing rules for staff. Later steps build on them. When each step has an owner and a checkpoint, progress becomes visible and problems appear early.

## How a roadmap improves your results

A roadmap reduces waste. You avoid buying tools before you know what they are for, and you avoid starting a second project while the first is unfinished. Budget is planned month by month, so there are no surprises when a bill arrives.

It also keeps people aligned. A manager can see why a step is happening now and not later. A team member knows what is expected of them. Checkpoints give you a clear moment to look at the evidence and choose again, which protects you from carrying on with something that is not working. Cost ranges are estimates, and results depend on how the work is carried out.

## What a good AI roadmap includes

- A clear statement of your goals and the problems you want to solve.
- A list of initiatives, kept to a number your team can really handle.
- A month by month order of work, with dependencies shown.
- A named owner for every step.
- A cost range for each step and a monthly budget view.
- Skills and training your team will need along the way.
- Risks, such as data quality, staff time and vendor dependence.
- Checkpoints that say when to continue, adjust or stop.
- Success measures for each initiative.
- A one page summary that anyone can read in a few minutes.

## How we prepare your roadmap

We begin with what we know about your business: your goals, your team, your tools and your budget. If you have an earlier audit or review, we build on it. If not, we gather what we need in a short conversation, and we ask about the tasks and constraints that will shape the order of work.

The Basic package gives a simple plan for a shorter period with the first steps, owners and a one page summary. Standard covers a longer period with more initiatives, cost ranges, risks, checkpoints and a planning call. Premium adds a monthly budget view, skills and training needs and success measures for each step. Add-ons include an extra planning call, a budget sheet and slides for people who need to approve the plan.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Choose a small number of initiatives and finish them.
- Give every step one clear owner.
- Put preparation steps, such as data tidy-up and staff rules, first.
- Review the plan at each checkpoint with the evidence in front of you.
- Share the one page summary with the whole team.

**Avoid:**
- Filling the plan with every idea you have heard about.
- Starting several large steps in the same month.
- Setting a budget without a cost range for each step.
- Treating the roadmap as fixed when circumstances change.
- Leaving staff training out of the plan.

## Who this is for

This service suits an owner who knows AI matters but does not know where to start or what to do second. It suits a manager who must present a plan and a budget to a partner or board. It also suits a business that has already tried a few tools and now wants a joined-up approach.

You do not need an audit first. An earlier audit makes the plan sharper, but we can work from a conversation and the information you already have.

## What we need from you

A short description of your goals, your team and any budget limit. Send any earlier reports, tool lists or notes you have. We never ask for passwords, because the roadmap is a planning document and needs no account access. If you want us to help carry out the plan afterwards, we can quote that separately.
